newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends $3.75 down, Brent hits day's low.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends $3.75 down, Brent hits day's low.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures closed down $3.75 a tonnne on Tuesday in line with weaker Brent crude and NYMEX products prices, traders said.
Front-month March gas oil settled at $163.25, $2.25 off the highs after trading in a range between $163.00 and $163.40 for the final two hours of business.
The March/April spread was stable in a $2 contango, with April settling at $165.25.
Gas oil came off in line with steady selling of April Brent, which was down 28 cents at a new session low of $19.00 a barrel at 1805 GMT against a fundamentally weak backdrop.
Traders saw NYMEX-inspired selling of the April/May Brent spread down to around five cents from around 40 cents and the May/June to minus one cent from around 20 cents ove the day.
May Brent, which takes over as the prompt contract next Monday, was 20 cents off at $18.95 a barrel.
"I don't think we're going to see any recovery given the state of the physical market," said a broker.
Cash market traders said the weight of unsold March crudes from the North Sea and West Africa were exacting a heavy toll.
Norwegian Gullfaks crude traded at a 42-cent discount to benchmark wet Brent on Tuesday, 27 cents weaker than on Friday.
Brokers were waiting for the release of latest U.S. inventory data due after the markets close on Tuesday for clues as to the next major move.
"The market could be heading for another push lower but it may wait until after the figures come out," said one, referring to the American Petroleum Institute (API) data due out later.
Immediate support on April Brent was seen at $18.95-$19.02 a barrel.
